items.title: Ypsilanti fights U-M $1.2B computing center on 144 Huron River acres
items.dek: University of Michigan plans a $1.2 billion high-performance computing facility on 144 acres it purchased last year next to the Huron River in eastern Washtenaw County, backed by a $100 million state grant and tied to Los Alamos National Laboratory national security research. Township leaders call the site selection offensive to their community of 54,000 with lower per-capita income and vow continued opposition over transparency and potential security risks.
items.findings: U-M affirmed Tuesday it will build $1.2B facility on 144 acres on Textile Road purchased last year for research computing serving U-M and Los Alamos | State approved $100M Strategic Site Readiness Program grant in December 2024 for the project | Township of 54,000 has $36,000 per-capita income versus $53,000 countywide; officials say location burdens poorer area | U-M says project could create 200 jobs that pay an average of $200,000 per year but township leaders call details unverified | Project labeled computing center to distinguish from hyperscale facilities; nearby Saline Township hosts $43B Oracle/OpenAI project | Township passed resolutions against it and encouraged year-long pause on data center approvals through Ypsilanti Community Utilities Authority
items.perspective: Township officials have mobilized against the project for the last year with resolutions and opposition; U-M schedules community town hall for Sept. 9 in the township. U-M spokesperson said center would not involve storage or handling of nuclear materials. U.S. Rep. Debbie Dingell criticized U-M for rebuffing community concerns and ignoring residents who do not want the project.
